claimBoundary: The source-generated cases bypass RGB-to-YCbCr conversion and encoder chroma downsampling by using libjpeg raw_data_in. Y is constant 128, Cr is constant 128, and Cb varies only by low-resolution row; the actual post-IDCT planes are then re-observed through libjpeg raw_data_out before any reconstruction analysis.

For both 4:4:0 and 4:2:0, the global-context model is the libjpeg 3/4-current + 1/4-adjacent vertical fancy rule across every row boundary. The iMCU-clamped model uses the same weights everywhere except that the last high-resolution row of each 16-row iMCU group may not read the next low-resolution row and the first row of the next group may not read the previous one.

Context topology is tested symmetrically and independently of backend-specific color rounding. For each backend, one affine blue-versus-reconstructed-Cb map is fit only from non-boundary output rows, where the two context models are identical. That frozen map is then evaluated on held-out phase-0/15 rows. libjpeg must prefer global context on those rows, while ImageCraft/ImageIO must prefer iMCU-clamped context, for both generated sampling modes. This is observational equivalence and does not assert knowledge of Apple's internal implementation.

The retained real-photo check does not fit a model. It only tests whether ImageIO-versus-libjpeg residuals are phase-localized at y mod 16 equal to 0 or 15, as independently predicted by the source-generated mechanism. No observed pixel delta is promoted into a production tolerance or perceptual-quality claim.
